Original text: To test the code, run `make test` in the source directory. This will exercise the unit tests (using [pytest](https://docs.pytest.org/)) and generate a coverage report.
Atomic rule: Run `make test` from the source directory to exercise the unit test suite.
Section context: The Testing section offers no alternative invocation and names no subset of the suite; the preceding sentence only covers installing the extra dependencies. `.github/workflows/ci.yaml`'s `run-tests` job runs `make test` on every supported Python version, and the `Makefile` expands it to `uv run --no-sync pytest -n auto --cov=seaborn --cov=tests --cov-config=pyproject.toml tests`.
Notes: Applies to any change to seaborn/ or tests/. The coverage report is a side effect of the target, not a separate obligation. Cross-ref: `Makefile` target `test`, `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` job `run-tests`.

Original text: Code style is enforced with `ruff` using the settings in the [`pyproject.toml`](./pyproject.toml) file.
Atomic rule: Make the changed Python files satisfy the ruff configuration declared in `pyproject.toml`.
Section context: The README delegates the content rather than restating it: `pyproject.toml` sets `[tool.ruff] line-length = 88`, `extend-exclude = ["seaborn/cm.py", "seaborn/external"]`, and `[tool.ruff.lint] select = ["E", "W", "F"]` with `ignore = ["E741", "F522"]`. The word 'enforced' is cashed out by the `lint` CI job, which runs `make lint` on every pull request to master. No exemption is offered anywhere on the page.
Notes: Extracted once as a conformance obligation rather than one row per ruff rule code. The pre-commit `ruff` hook carries no `--fix` argument, so nothing repairs a violation before the patch exists. Cross-ref: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` job `lint`.

Atomic rule: Run `make lint` locally to check the change against the project's ruff settings.
Section context: The immediately following sentence sanctions a different route: "Alternately, you can use `pre-commit` to automatically run lint checks on any files you are committing". The preceding sentence supplies the scope: "Code style is enforced with `ruff` using the settings in the [`pyproject.toml`](./pyproject.toml) file."
Notes: Distinct from MWASKOM-C002: that rule is a static read of the diff against the ruff config, this one is a trajectory read of whether the check was invoked. Not a duplicate. The `Makefile` expands the target to `uv run --no-sync ruff check seaborn/ tests/`.

Original text: Alternately, you can use `pre-commit` to automatically run lint checks on any files you are committing: just run `pre-commit install` to set it up, and then commit as usual going forward.
Atomic rule: Install the pre-commit hooks with `pre-commit install` when using pre-commit rather than `make lint` to check style.
Section context: "Alternately, you can" frames the whole clause as one of two permitted routes, the other being `make lint`. `.pre-commit-config.yaml` decides what installing actually buys: `end-of-file-fixer` and `trailing-whitespace` rewrite files during the commit, while the `ruff` hook runs without `--fix` and only reports.
Notes: Applies only if the contributor opts for pre-commit instead of `make lint`; the choice is the contributor's own, not the task's. Cross-ref: MWASKOM-C003, which this sentence is the sanctioned alternative to.

Original text: But please be aware that current development efforts are mostly focused on standardizing the API and internals, and there may be relatively low enthusiasm for novel features that do not fit well into short- and medium-term development plans.
Atomic rule: Keep a proposed change aligned with the current focus on standardizing the API and internals rather than adding a novel feature.
Section context: The preceding sentence invites the contributor in rather than shutting them out: "If you think there is a new feature that should be added to seaborn, you can open an issue to discuss it." The section states no criterion, no list of accepted areas and no consequence; 'short- and medium-term development plans' are not published anywhere in the repository.
Notes: The only clause in `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md` that a diff rather than an issue body could violate. Its first sentence is X-ISSUE and produces no row.
